svg.text: Photos see the canopy; pulses reach the ground through the gaps
A leaf stops a laser pulse just as it blocks a camera's view. The difference is the holes between leaves: a pulse that finds one keeps going.
Photographs: the surface is the canopy top
LiDAR: some pulses find a gap
red: ground that no photo ever saw
the model there is a guess copied from the canopy
every camera ray stops at the first leaf
stopped by a leaf: a canopy return
through a gap: a ground return
here: 20 pulses over the crowns, 4 reached the ground
a leaf is not transparent; the pulse went between leaves
Photographs: 0 ground points under the crowns
the ground has to be seen in two photos to be modelled
plenty for a terrain model on a 1 m grid
Dense evergreen canopy leaves few gaps; bare winter branches leave many, so a deciduous site maps best with the leaves off.
